newsitem.title: UK: U.S. venture to offer Airbus jumbo power.
newsitem.headline: U.S. venture to offer Airbus jumbo power.

text.p: U.S. aero-engine joint venture GE-P&W Engine Alliance will offer its new engine to the European Airbus Industrie consortium, although the powerplant is being developed for Boeing superjumbo.

A GE Aircraft Engines spokesman said at the Farnborough air show on Monday it will "definitely offer" the GP7176 engine to Airbus if it builds its 3XX superjumbo, which would seat over 500 passengers.

GE Aircraft Engines, a unit of General Electric, and Pratt & Whitney, a unit of United Technologies Corp, formed the Engine Alliance to build an engine for the Boeing 747-500X and 600X planes which are bigger derivatives of the 747 jumbo jet.
The development cost of the new engine is $1 billion, which shared equally between the firms, which would have otherwise spent that amount separately, the spokesman said.
The GP7176 develops thrust between 70,000 to 80,000 pounds.
